status: Meets the Bench Standard bar on Opus (no invented facts in any run). On Haiku it beats every comparison and scores 62/67 consistently, but 2-4 of 10 evals per round still contain a widened or added claim; recommended for larger models.
method: 10 evals (4 traps), expectations written before any run. Each run is a fresh headless agent that never saw the expectations, graded blind by a separate grader. Round 1 compared the skill, no skill and the comparison skill (the author's de-slop) on Haiku; round 5 compared Opus with and without the skill. Rounds 2-9 re-ran the skill as it was revised. Four 'no new facts' expectations were tightened before round 5 to count only facts confirmed in brand/ (stricter for every config).
losses_and_open_issues: Haiku v1.5.0: widened or added claims in 2-4 evals per round. The swapped-noun check removed the 'prime cost' swaps, but Haiku still hardens verbs ('helping reduce no-shows' to 'reduces no-shows'), adds evaluative lines ('No hidden layers'), and reuses a voice example as a promise
Haiku explains a wrong price inconsistently (corrects $299 to $349 but doesn't always say $299 is the group rate)
Haiku sometimes doesn't list removed statistics as 'needing a source', and its 'What changed' lists can misdescribe the draft
Opus v1.4.0's about-page rebuild ran 69 words against a 67-word original (expectation: shorter)
No-skill Opus overwrote the user's drafts and left placeholders in final copy; the skill never touched an original in 90 runs
